To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

gene essentiality prediction algorithms that combine essentiality data across genes are the most accurate; gene expression data is the most informative molecular feature for predicting essentialities; well-predictified genes and selected molecular feaures are enriched for functional categories; and selected features correlate with survival in primary tumor.

(1) the best predictors of gene essentialities were those that integrated data from multiple genes; (2) gene expression was the molecular feature with the most predictive power; (3) the best performing predictors were those that used the same gene as their target; (4) the predictors that were most accurate for predicting essentiality of one gene were not necessarily those most accurate for another gene; (5) the best predictors for a given gene tended to predict the same essentiality for the majority of

gene essentiality is a highly heritable property that can be predicted from gene expression and other molecular data, and that the ability to make these predictions is a function of the gene being tested.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genes and pathways that are essential for the survival of cancer cells.
the development and evaluation of computational models to predict the relative essentiality of genes in cancer cells.
the development of computational methods for the inference of gene essentiality from large functional genetic screens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the DREAM Challenge has demonstrated that the ability to predict the relative importance of genes in a cancer cell line is possible and has identified a number of important factors that can improve the accuracy of such predictions.
the challenge was a success in the sense of providing the community with a benchmark and a resource, and in the sense of stimulating research and providing a framework for a community-wide effort.

this study establishes benchmarks for predicting gene essentiality from genetic perturbation screens, provides a community resource for comparison with this benchmark and provides insights into the factors influencing the ability for prediction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this study demonstrates the value of open research collaborations and that we have established a benchmark for gene essentiality prediction.
this study establishes benchmarks for predicting gene essentiality from genetic screens and that it demonstrates the value of engaging the community in an early stage of research.
this is the first time we have seen the DREAM community come together to solve a real problem, and the first time that a community has been able to solve a real-world problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gene expression is an important predictor of gene essentiality and that gene essentiality prediction is more accurate when multiple genes are analyzed together.
the DREAM challenge is a powerful way to engage a large number of computational researchers in solving a complex biological problem.
the community can achieve a high level of performance in predicting gene essentiality from a novel functional genetic screen.
